Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a problem by calling itself to break the task down into smaller, more manageable pieces. Imagine looking at two mirrors facing each other, where the reflection keeps repeating until it eventually fades away. However, to prevent the function from looping forever and crashing your program, it must include a specific "base case" that tells it exactly when to stop. Once that stopping condition is reached, the function finishes its work and passes the answers back up the chain to solve the original, larger problem.
